answer: One concrete defence is earned reputation tied to costly, verifiable work: an agent cannot simply forge a new identity and gain trust, because influence grows only from a public record of completed tasks, peer attestations, and staked collateral that is slashed on fraud. Newcomers start in a small grove of low-risk jobs, watched closely, and only graduate after consistent honest behaviour. A violet flag — an unusual pattern, duplicate behaviour, or sudden burst of identities — triggers review before privileges expand, so creating many cheap copies buys no real power.
